'''Alabama white sauce''' is a variety of mayonnaise-based white barbecue sauce. Its origin is frequently traced to Robert Gibson of Big Bob Gibson’s Bar-B-Q restaurant in Alabama<ref>https://heygrillhey.com/alabama-white-sauce/</ref><ref>https://www.chilipeppermadness.com/recipes/white-bbq-sauce/</ref><ref>https://www.southernkissed.com/alabama-white-barbecue-sauce/</ref><ref>https://bigbobgibson.com/</ref>. The sauce can be brushed on meat or used as a dipping sauce. 

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayonnaise]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] apple [[Cookbook:Cider Vinegar|cider vinegar]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Corn Syrup|corn syrup]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]]
* Prepared [[Cookbook:Horseradish|horseradish]]
* [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|Lemon juice]]
* Salt
* [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|Black pepper]]

== Procedure ==
#Place all ingredients in a very large [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] or [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]]. Blend for 1 minute, or until thoroughly combined and mixture is smooth. Pour sauce into a large bowl.
#Use when grilling chicken or other poultry or meat; [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] lightly over the chicken (or meat) during the last few minutes of grilling. This sauce is also great for dipping; set some sauce aside for passing at the table.
